commits.subject: Never show an unasked SSH or WSL offer long after it stopped being true
Offer a destination again when its unseen offer was replaced by another

items.how: Reproduced first on BASE: the reviewer's scenario failed. A held "Can't connect to build-01", the ssh to web-07 ends, and Close is pressed 45 minutes later: "You're connected to web-07" then shows. The WSL first-seen offer behaved the same way. Cause: showSeenOffer and offerWsl post with { ms: OFFER_MS, claim: "reply" }. Presenter.armHide only stores pendingHide while the bubble is unseen, so nothing limited how long an offer could wait. Fix, in app/main/targets/runtime.ts and app/main/targets/offer.ts: (1) Both unasked offers now go through a new postUnasked(). It arms a runtime timer of OFFER_MS at post time. If the offer is still on its board and the board's shownAt is still null (it never reached the screen), the offer is cleared from the board and let go unseen. For a seen-ssh offer that means offers.delete(k) and noticer.release(seenKey). For the WSL offer it means wslOffered = false. The noticer's next look (a new terminal title), or the next request that names WSL, can then offer it again while it still holds. (2) After every process read that worked, the noticer calls the new NoticerDeps.running(keys) with the seenKeys of every user ssh running now. The runtime's sshRunning withdraws any seen offer, on screen or waiting, whose ssh has ended, and releases its key if nobody saw it. A process list that can't be read reports nothing. (3) A later offer can replace an unasked offer on the offers board before it ever showed (another ssh, or offer_connect's Connect). That offer is now let go the same way, so its destination isn't used up unseen. Offers the user asked for (offer_connect) are unchanged. The time an offer stays on screen (25 s, 250 s with More time) is unchanged. The wait limit is a flat OFFER_MS and is not scaled by More time, because a waiting offer isn't being read. The X3 Lost test now presses Stop trying 21 s in, inside the 25 s limit (it used to wait 60 s). Docs: docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §3.1 and §4.1, and CHANGELOG.md, now say an unasked offer waits 25 seconds at most, goes unseen when its ssh has ended, and comes again if it was never seen. The phrase test/unit/docs.test.ts checks is kept. Remaining edge, by design: on screen, an offer whose ssh ends is withdrawn only when the noticer next looks, which needs a terminal title change and at most one look every 10 s. So it can still show for up to 25 s after the session ended if the user leaves the terminal. Note: the reviewer's own scratch file still fails as written, because its rig's parts.setTimeout never fires on its own. With that file copied in and the runtime timers run after the 45-minute advance, it passes.

The new NoticerDeps.running doc and both commit bodies say "a list that can't be read reports nothing", but that only holds when the whole local list fails. The runtime's noticeOf (app/main/targets/runtime.ts, the userSshProcesses wrapper above `let noticer`) still returns `local` when `w.runningNow()` throws. commits.subject: Never show an unasked SSH or WSL offer long after it stopped being true
Offer a destination again when its unseen offer was replaced by another
Keep an SSH offer up while Ember couldn't read where its ssh runs
Say that an unasked SSH offer goes at Ember's next look, up or waiting

items.how:
First pass (15fd5ec, 139856d), unchanged. An unasked offer (a seen ssh, or "I can work in WSL") goes through postUnasked. It waits OFFER_MS at most after it is posted. If it never reached the screen by then, it goes unseen and is released, so the next look, or the next request that names WSL, can offer it again. An unasked offer that another offer replaces before it showed is released the same way. After each look, the noticer reports which of the user's ssh run now, and sshRunning withdraws a seen offer whose ssh has ended, whether it is up or waiting. Offers the user asked for, and the time an offer stays on screen, are unchanged.

Second pass, verifier problem 1 (partial reads; fec8a25). The verifier is right. I reproduced it at HEAD 139856d with a test that failed for each failure mode: `exit: / reject: / running: expected { visible: false … } to match object { visible: true … }`. Each look now reports what it read in full, and an offer goes only when its ssh is missing from a place that look read.
- app/main/targets/offer.ts: SshNotice.userSshProcesses takes an optional `read: Set<string>`, which the reader fills with each WSL place (`wsl:<distro>`) it read in full. The noticer passes it whenever it passes `wsl`. NoticerDeps.running is now `running(keys, read: (via) => boolean)`. The local list is read whole or not at all (null means no call). A WSL distro counts as read only if the reader named it. Its doc and the file header now say exactly that, which replaces the old wording "a list that can't be read reports nothing". The earlier commit bodies can't be changed without rewriting history, so fec8a25's body corrects that claim.
- app/main/targets/runtime.ts, noticeOf: a distro whose reader returned code 0 is added to `read`. So is a distro that is not in `live`: it is stopped, so its ssh really has ended, and it is not read or started. Nothing is added when runningNow throws, when the runner throws or isn't WA's, or when runScript rejects or exits non-zero.
- sshRunning(keys, read) skips any seen offer whose `o.seen.via` wasn't read.
- SA's userSshProcessesWith in app/main/remote/notice-ssh.ts still drops a failed distro silently. That no longer matters. The runtime never passes `wsl` to it (the existing test asserts `toHaveBeenCalledWith("win32")`), and it never fills `read`, so an ssh it reads in WSL is never taken as ended. This fails closed, and a noticer test covers it.
- Same class of bug, also fixed: every SA parser stops at SSH_MAX = 64 ssh per place. A list that comes back at that cap may have been cut short, so the noticer doesn't count it as read. SSH_MAX is now exported from notice-ssh.ts; the only change there is that export and its doc line.

Verifier problem 2 (docs wording; 21601f5). The verifier is right.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.1 now reads: "…one that couldn't show by then goes unseen. The next time Ember looks, an offer whose `ssh` it finds has ended goes too, whether it is up or still waiting. It offers each computer once per run (again, the next time it looks, if you never saw the offer)…". "Finds" covers a look that couldn't read the distro. The block is reflowed to the paragraph's width: lines 445-449 are now 112, 108, 110, 114 and 93 characters, and the 153-character line is gone.
- CHANGELOG.md now reads: "…but 25 seconds at most, and it goes, up or waiting, the next time Ember looks and finds the `ssh` it names has ended." It is reflowed with the next four lines at 120 characters, which the file already uses, and the rest of the bullet is unchanged.
- §4.1 line 434 already says when Ember looks (a terminal title change, at most every 10 seconds).
- The phrase test/unit/docs.test.ts checks (§4.1, "An offer to work on another computer that you didn't ask for waits while…") is unchanged.

Remaining edge, not fixed (it needs SA's reader to report truncation): linuxSshProcesses scans only the first 5000 /proc entries (SCAN_MAX) and doesn't say when it stopped early. On a machine with about 5000 or more processes, an ssh beyond that point could be taken as ended. Desktops rarely run that many processes.

The verifier was right on both problems. Nothing was disputed.

Design choice: rather than keeping shared state between noticeOf and sshRunning, the noticer passes an out-set (`read`) to the process read and hands a predicate to running(keys, read). The contract is positive: a place counts as read only if the reader names it. A reader that names nothing (SA's own, or any fake) therefore never causes a WSL offer to be withdrawn. Only this computer's list counts as read without being named, because it is read whole or not at all.

items.how: I confirmed the problem against BASE: HandleWindow.corner() always used workArea x+width-size-12 (bottom right), the overlay anchored .tasks to the right, there was no setting, and the copy hard-coded "bottom-right corner". Built per D-75. (1) New app/shared/handle-place.ts holds the pure, Electron-free logic: HANDLE_POSITIONS, sideOf, otherSide, and handleCorner(position, size, workArea), which places the window 12 px in from the work area's bottom and right or left edge. settings.ts gains handlePosition: z.enum(HANDLE_POSITIONS).default("bottom-right"). The settings version stays 1: a file from before the setting reads as bottom-right and is not rewritten, and a bad value is repaired on its own. Like the other comfort settings, an organisation's policy cannot manage it. (2) HandleWindow.corner() reads the setting. The pill, the 56x56 hidden-state tab and the no-compositor card all follow it inside the primary display's work area. sendSettings() moves the window and returns true when the position changed, so main moves the desk view with it. (3) main.ts: the handle menu gets { label: "Move to the other side", click: moveHandle } after Hide/Show Ember. moveHandle flips the setting with otherSide() through settings.update; a failed save is logged as handle.move_not_saved and nothing moves. The settings listener now moves the handle before the overlays hear the change, and OverlayManager.broadcastSettings() calls checkHandle(), so the overlays get the handle's new place at once instead of on the next 1 s check. (4) Overlay: layout.ts adds handleSide() (taken from where the pill is on this display, otherwise from the setting) and stackPlace() (the inset and bottom, lined up with the pill's outer edge). cardsCorner() takes the handle's side and returns the other bottom corner while a control's ring is under the cards. overlay/main.ts toggles .tasks.left, renames cardsLeft to cardsAway and re-places the stack when the side changes. styles.css adds .tasks.left { right: auto; left: 12px; }. (5) Copy: home/copy.ts handleCornerText(), and tagline() takes the corner. In index.html, Comfort & access > Ember on screen gets a 'Handle position' select (Bottom right / Bottom left) and a hint, and "bottom-right corner" in the Your Ember hint is now a span. home/main.ts shows and saves the setting and updates the corner span, the tagline and the no-compositor presence line; that line is a live region, so it is set only when its words change. Found by tracing the side effects: the Linux desk view (desk/view.ts) sized itself to the room left of the handle, so with a bottom-left handle it shrank to a 1x1 window (a test reproduced it). deskViewBounds now mirrors the layout when the handle is bottom-left, deskViewStart() opens the view in the corner away from the handle, and handleMoved() moves it to the side the handle left. Checked but not changed: ask.ts clearOf falls back to the left of the handle only when the box can't fit above it, which needs a work area under about 296 px, so I left it alone. findings.title: Signing out while a startup renewal is in flight is undone: the renewed sign-in is saved again and Ember reconnects with it
findings.scenario: Ember's own GitHub App token is stored and ran out overnight, so the next start renews it before use. startBrain (main.ts ~1985) awaits keeper.freshen(), and findToken (Check again, the GitHub CLI wait) does the same. freshen() sends the refresh_token request. While that request is out, the user clicks Sign out in settings, which opens at a normal start. The IPC.signOut handler (main.ts 1215-1226) calls tokens.clear(), sets currentToken = null, calls keeper.use(null) and agent.start(null). Then GitHub answers. freshen() then calls store.saveAsync(next) without checking that the sign-in it renewed is still the one stored: it writes the renewed grant back to github-token.bin and sets it as held. startBrain goes on to resolveToken(tokens, ...), which now returns the resurrected token with source "stored", and connectWith(found, "auto") calls agent.start with it. host.start's signedOut flag only blocks environment and GitHub CLI tokens, so the stored one connects. The user is signed back in to the account they just left, and its token is on disk for every later start. A related case: when the renewal request is slow (a connection stuck across a network change) and the user signs in with the device flow as another account meanwhile, freshen's save overwrites the new account's grant, and startBrain then switches Copilot to the old account. The device-flow handler's comment says a renewal finishing meanwhile is "neither switched to nor saved". That holds for GrantKeeper.renew(), which checks this.grant and inUse, but not for freshen().
findings.evidence: I reproduced it with a scratch test, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix3-review/safety/tree/test/unit/zz-safety-signout.test.ts (run with `npx vitest run test/unit/zz-safety-signout.test.ts` in that tree). It stores an expired grant, starts keeper.freshen() with a fetch held open, then calls store.clear() and keeper.use(null) as sign-out does, then lets the fetch answer. Output: `SCRATCH after sign-out, saved: false`, then `SCRATCH after the renewal finished, saved: true token: ghu_bb`, then `SCRATCH resolveToken after sign-out: stored true`. In the code, freshen() (auth.ts 517-535) does `const next = await this.renewed(g); const kept = await store.saveAsync(next);` with no turn, epoch or stored-token check after the await. saveAsync takes its epoch only when it is called, after clear(), so the epoch guard doesn't help. renew() (auth.ts 588-605) does have `if (this.grant !== grant || this.d.inUse() !== grant.token) return;`.
findings.fix: In freshen(), note the keeper's turn (or a store generation such as TokenStore.epoch) before renewing. After `await this.renewed(g)`, save only if no use(), stop(), clear() or save happened meanwhile and the store still holds g.token (re-read it with loadGrant). Otherwise drop the renewed grant, or revoke it. In main.ts startBrain and findToken, don't connect with a "stored" token when a sign-out happened after the look began (check agent signedOut state, or a sign-out counter, after freshen and resolveToken).

findings.title: A crashed command window page keeps R7's approve-key guard "in view" and its countdown running while the page is blank (up to a minute per crash)
findings.scenario: Commit 71d6b0a changed createCommandWindow from closeWhenGone(win) to revive(win). A crashed page is no longer destroyed: it is reloaded after 500 ms, then after 1 s, 2 s and so on up to 60 s if it keeps crashing. The controller never hears of the crash. Example: a command card (ask) is up, the user has seen it and the page has reported cardSeen {inView: true}. The page then crashes, for example from hostile or huge output in a tab. The window stays visible and on top with a blank page. cardReady(n) still returns true, because view.inView is stale and live(), isVisible() and isAlwaysOnTop() all hold. So the approve key (Ctrl+Alt+Y, or its fallback) allows the command while the window shows nothing, until the reloaded page measures again, which can be up to a minute away with the backoff. This breaks R7's 'only while that window shows all of it'. In the same way, an announcement (D4.4) whose countdown started, or starts during the crash, counts down and runs while the command window is blank. startHead only checks live(), and the doc comment removed in 71d6b0a said a crashed window used to cancel the countdown. Impact is limited: 'seen' was true before the crash, and the bubble still shows the announcement's Stop.
findings.evidence: windows.ts createCommandWindow (after 71d6b0a): `revive(win);` replaces `closeWhenGone(win)`. revive.ts reloads after `delay`, which doubles up to 60_000. commands/window.ts cardReady (651-657) returns `w.isVisible() && !w.isMinimized() && (w.isAlwaysOnTop() || w.isFocused())` once `view.inView` is true. view is only changed by cardSeen messages, showCard and hideCard, and window.ts has no render-process-gone or did-start-loading listener (grep finds none). startHead (503-511) starts the timer whenever live() is non-null. The old closeWhenGone doc comment listed 'a countdown is cancelled' among what a crash did, and the new comment drops it.
findings.fix: Have the command window controller hear the page going away (pass revive an onGone callback, or listen to render-process-gone and did-start-loading). When it does, set view to {n, seen, inView: false} so cardReady is false until the reloaded page reports again. Also pause an announcement's countdown, or settle it as not run, while the page is down, as the destroyed window used to.

findings.title: A long typed text can't be read before its question runs out: the 2-minute question time ignores the whole-text block
findings.scenario: A task types a long text, which type_text and set_value both allow up to 5000 characters (worker.ts:1080, 1093), into the user's app. 'More time to read and answer' is off. The question shows all 4999 characters in the bubble's 7-line block. A keyboard user pages through with the approve key, which moves one page of about 6 lines (about 270 characters at the default size, about 200 at Larger). That takes 18 to 25 presses. Reading that much at 180 to 250 words a minute takes 4 to 5 minutes, and a screen reader takes as long to speak the live region's 'The whole text: …' announcement. After 2 minutes the question expires as 'Not now' while the user is still reading or listening, and the step is refused. The docs promise 'Screen readers hear all of it' and that Allow works once you have read it.
findings.evidence: confirm.ts:283 sets the expiry once, when the question shows: `p.timer = setTimeout(() => this.finish(p, null), this.timeout())`. main.ts:1718 sets `timeoutMs: () => 120_000 * readTime()`. answerKey's paging and wholeSeen() call this.show() again but never touch p.timer, and the timeout doesn't depend on detail's length. findings.title: On Windows (and likely macOS) the ask box now always has the keyboard before the quick context is read, so 'Focused:' and 'Selected text:' drop out of the ask context
findings.scenario: Windows: the user selects a sentence in Word or Notepad and presses Win+Alt+Space, then types 'make this bold'. openAsk takes the user's window (userWindowsNow, main.ts:1012), then openAskInOrder calls show() before read(active) (ask-open.ts:36-37). show() runs reveal() synchronously: win.show(), win.focus() and takeFocus, which on Windows calls inputRef.activate(id) and focusInput(id) (main.ts:914-918). Only after that does the readWindow request go to the host. The host's UIA walk reads HasKeyboardFocus, which is system-wide keyboard focus and is false for every element of the user's window once the box is foreground. With no focused node, the host asks no element for its selection, and quickContextText writes neither the 'Focused:' line nor 'Selected text:'. Windows has no PRIMARY-selection fallback (platform.clipboard is null on win32 and darwin). The request's context therefore names only the app and window, not what 'this' is. macOS's AXFocused probably behaves the same once the non-activating panel is key; I did not verify that on a real Mac.
findings.evidence: ask-open.ts:28-38: `o.show(); o.read(active);` when an active window was taken (always on Windows and macOS, since keyboardHold is null there). main.ts:914-918: takeFocus calls `inputRef?.activate(id); inputRef?.focusInput?.(id)` inside reveal(), i.e. before read(). app/sidecar-host/providers/uia.ts:142: `set("focused", b.hasKeyboardFocus)`. app/sidecar-host/tree.ts:188-215: `wants.selection` is set only `if (focused)`. app/main/perception/index.ts:913-923: quickContextText takes focus and selection only from focusedElement(seen.nodes). win32/platform.ts:70 and darwin/platform.ts:58: `clipboard: null`, so Perception.withSelection adds nothing. At 9912de5, captureContext() was dispatched before askWindow.show(), so this was already a race that the walk often lost on Windows. typeahead2 makes the loss certain. No integration test checks quickContext on any OS (grep for quickContext / 'Selected text' under test/integration finds nothing). The worker can still re-read the screen once the box closes, so nothing becomes unusable; the initial context and the box's 'Ember will see' line lose the selection.
findings.fix: Before show() on Windows and macOS, take the focused element and its selection cheaply. For example, have userWindowsNow also ask the host or input layer for the focused element (UIA FocusedElement with its TextPattern selection, or AX AXFocusedUIElement with AXSelectedText) and pass it into quickContext. Alternatively, have the read in quickContext take the window's last-focused element (UIA: the element whose hwnd is the window's GUI-thread focus; AX: the app's AXFocusedUIElement, which survives deactivation) instead of the per-node HasKeyboardFocus/AXFocused state. Add an ember-win32 integration check that a selection made in the bench before the ask chord shows up in the ask context.

findings.title: The smoke test's '--ask opened the ask box' check passes without the box ever showing

At main.ts:1030 the line is logged after openAskInOrder whatever AskWindow.show() did: when the prepared page isn't loaded yet, show() only sets `wanted` (ask.ts: `if (this.loaded) this.reveal(...)`), and the box is dropped if ready-to-show comes more than LATE_MS (1.5 s) later. findings.title: A start by the launcher's Ask Ember keeps --ask in argv, so 'Restart Ember' and the policy restart reopen the ask box unasked
findings.scenario: RHEL 8: Ember isn't running and the user clicks Ask Ember in the GNOME dash (packaging/ember.desktop `Exec=ember --ask`), or Ask Ember in the Windows jump list. That first instance's process.argv holds `--ask` for its whole life. Later, an RPM update lands and the user picks 'Restart Ember', or the administrator's policy changes and the user restarts. restartAfterUpdate calls app.relaunch() with no options, which reuses process.argv. The AppImage and policy paths (restartOptions) pass argv.slice(1). Either way the new process starts with --ask. startView returns 'ask', so the box pops open over whatever the user is doing, takes the keyboard, and the greeting after the restart is skipped. The one-off 'open the box now' intent is replayed as if the user had just asked.
